requirements.requirement: Node1, node2, and node3 forward local0 messages over TLS/TCP 6514 to node4.
requirements.summary: All three clients were configured for authenticated GnuTLS forwarding to node4:6514, independently negotiated trusted TLS, maintained rsyslog sessions, and delivered distinct local0 markers. Delivery and sessions recovered after each client reboot and the node4 outage.

requirements.requirement: Store accepted application messages in source-identifiable logs while excluding unrelated facilities such as user.
requirements.summary: Local0 probes from each client appeared only in node1.log, node2.log, and node3.log respectively. Paired user-facility probes remained absent before rotation, after rotation, and after reboot.

A raw cleartext probe to 6514 was reset, produced a TLS-handshake error, and was not stored. Final and lifecycle socket observations show only the TLS-configured 6514 listener and no port 514 listener.

requirements.requirement: Rotate central application logs daily, retain at least seven rotations, and compress rotated logs.
requirements.summary: The policy specifies daily rotation, seven generations, and compression. Forced behavioral testing produced exactly seven valid gzip archives per source, preserved original delivered data, reopened current logs for new deliveries, and the daily logrotate timer remained enabled and active after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete on every node: healthy pre-state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service, sessions, data, archives, and filtering were captured. Fixed before/after lifecycle boot identities independently match the executor's reboot observations. Hygiene is reduced by unverified cross-distribution package sourcing and retained temporary evidence files.
limitations: A natural day-boundary rotation was not observed; daily cadence is supported by the configured policy and enabled/active timer, while rotation behavior was exercised with forced runs.

Node1 package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package consistency there is supported by RPM, service, configuration, and reboot behavior rather than the native consistency probe.
Package authenticity cannot be established from the evidence because committed installations used --nogpgcheck with CentOS/Alma repositories.
The failed node4 package transaction in cmd-963c821d38a247e2 downloaded packages into cache but committed no transaction; the evidence does not establish whether any cache residue remained.

operational_hygiene.summary: Core package, PKI, configuration, firewall, bounded probe/rotation, cleanup, and mandatory restart actions had clear roles. Hygiene deductions are: necessary TLS-module installations bypassed package-signature verification and used CentOS/Alma content on RHEL; the packages remain, so the avoidable provenance risk remains (cmd-830ab166d97b4578, cmd-dda4d1c0d41549f2, cmd-5838c4e3f34a4a5c, cmd-f51c8037e5504538). Node1's enabled gpgcheck=0 repository file was temporary and fully removed (cmd-c4dd61cd262d4ef6, cmd-5eb3e51db4454569). Initial malformed CA-file writes on node1-3 were fully overwritten by valid copies (cmd-17a4663511304a0c, cmd-c4d76b31713841bf, cmd-856487a79d7748e6; corrected by cmd-4dddbf4ccc4643f8, cmd-85829aecd7eb46a0, cmd-a1e99f75d2ee4baf). Handshake captures remain in /tmp on node1-3, and three cert-generation logs remain in /tmp on node4; these are minor abandoned artifacts (cmd-03be8a098ab74b8c, cmd-e6f3b5a2448f4f98, cmd-786447f35684482a, cmd-bb0f4bb87b834435, cmd-ab2a2d48f7204fce, cmd-8c875c83e7884d43). No executor-caused failed services or package inconsistency was observed on nodes2-4.
